aboutPage.h1: A small note from the family behind qr-cow.
aboutPage.intro: qr-cow is a free QR code generator with logo, colors, gradients, dynamic codes, scan analytics, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, built by the HSN family, a small group of engineers who ship honest tools for the open web. There is no VC deck, no growth team, no marketing department. Just one project among many that we ship with love.
aboutPage.who1: The HSN family is a real family. All of us work in tech. Between us we ship side projects across the web, small, focused tools that try to be honest about what they do. qr-cow is one of those.
aboutPage.who2: We are not a brand pretending to be a person, and not a person pretending to be a brand. We are a family that likes building things, and shipping them where they will be useful.
aboutPage.started1: In late 2025 a friend opened a small café. She paid a designer to print her menu with a QR code on the bottom. Two weeks later she changed the menu, but the QR still pointed at the old PDF. She paid the designer again. Then again. After the third reprint we wrote her a script, one short URL she could edit herself, and the printed code kept working.
aboutPage.started2: That script became this site. The mascot is a cow because the placeholder we drew while testing the studio happened to look like one, and removing it felt wrong.
aboutPage.careCheapBody: Real analytics for $3 a month, not $19 a month. Indies and small teams should not be subsidising sales reps they will never talk to.
aboutPage.carePortableBody: Static codes work with no account. Designs export as SVG. If you ever outgrow qr-cow, you take everything with you.
aboutPage.carePrivateBody: We run our own analytics. Nothing leaks to Google, Facebook, or anyone else.
aboutPage.careCryptoBody: Cards do not really work where some of us live, and chargebacks on three-dollar subscriptions are not a business worth running.

docsPage.authBody: Send Authorization: Bearer qrc_live_… on every request. Tokens are universal, they work against every endpoint a session JWT does. Revoked tokens are rejected immediately.
docsPage.errorsBody: All responses follow '{success, data, error}'. HTTP status codes match RFC 7231; the error field carries a short machine-readable code (e.g. token_limit_reached).
docsPage.readsDesc: Listing, fetching, and analytics reads are not rate-limited.

docsPage.rateNote: Limits are keyed by IP and no rate-limit headers are sent, so on a 429 (error "rate_limit_exceeded") back off and retry. We only store the SHA-256 of each token; revoke immediately if one leaks and provision a fresh one in seconds.

url.title: Free URL QR code generator
url.sub: Turn any web address into a scannable QR code. Paste a URL, pick a style, download as PNG, SVG, or JPG, no signup, no expiration, no watermark.
url.metaDescription: Free URL QR code generator. Convert any website link to a scannable QR with logo, colors, and gradients. PNG / SVG / JPG export. No signup.

faq.q: Does the URL QR code expire?
faq.a: No. Static URL codes encode the destination directly into the pattern. Once you download the QR, it works forever without depending on qr-cow's servers.

faq.q: Can I change the URL after I print the code?
faq.a: Only with a dynamic code. Save the QR to a free account and pick Dynamic, you can then edit the destination any time without reprinting the QR. Static codes are free; dynamic codes are $3/month.

faq.q: Do long URLs make the QR harder to scan?
faq.a: Yes, longer URLs produce a denser, harder-to-scan code. For long tracking URLs (with UTM parameters) use a dynamic code: qr-cow shortens the destination internally so the printed pattern stays simple while you keep the full attribution server-side.

wifi.title: Free Wi-Fi QR code generator
wifi.sub: Print a sticker that joins guests onto your Wi-Fi without anyone typing the password. Enter your SSID + password, pick a style, download, works on every modern phone's camera.
wifi.metaDescription: Free Wi-Fi QR code generator, guests scan and join your network automatically. WPA / WEP / open networks supported. No signup.

faq.q: Which phones can join Wi-Fi from a QR code?
faq.a: Every iPhone running iOS 11+ and every Android running 10+ can join a Wi-Fi network by pointing the camera at a QR code, no app required. Older phones may need a free QR reader app.

faq.q: Is it safe to print my Wi-Fi password as a QR code?
faq.a: The QR code is literally a printed copy of the password. Fine for a café guest network; not fine for your corporate admin network. Use a dedicated guest VLAN with its own password if you're posting the code publicly.

faq.q: Does it work if my SSID is hidden?
faq.a: Yes. Tick "Hidden network" when generating, the QR will include the hidden flag so the scanning phone knows to look for the SSID instead of waiting for it to broadcast.

vcard.title: Free vCard QR code generator
vcard.sub: A vCard QR puts your contact info straight into a phone's address book in two taps. Add it to your business card, slide deck, or trade-show badge, recipients save you without typing a thing.
vcard.metaTitle: Free vCard / Business Card QR Code Generator
vcard.metaDescription: Free vCard QR code generator. Encode name, phone, email, company, title, website, save to phone contacts in two taps. No signup.

faq.q: vCard vs MeCard, which should I use?
faq.a: Default to vCard. It's the international standard, supports more fields (company, title, website, addresses), and every modern phone recognises it. MeCard is shorter (so the QR is smaller) but loses fields, only worth the trade when the printed code has to be tiny.

faq.q: Can I update my vCard QR if I change jobs?
faq.a: Static vCards bake the contact info into the printed pattern, so a new role means a new QR. If you change jobs often, use a dynamic code that points at a contact page you can update, the printed code stays valid.

faq.q: Will the contact save to iPhone AND Android?
faq.a: Yes. Both iOS and Android recognise vCard QRs natively and prompt the user with "Add to Contacts". The same QR works for both, no separate codes needed.

mecard.title: Free MeCard QR code generator
mecard.sub: MeCard is the shorter, Japanese-standard sibling of vCard, encodes the same essentials (name, phone, email) into a smaller, denser QR. Useful when the printed code must be tiny.
mecard.metaDescription: Free MeCard QR code generator, compact contact QR for tiny print surfaces. Smaller than vCard, recognised by every modern phone.

faq.q: When should I pick MeCard over vCard?
faq.a: Only when print space is genuinely tight, sticker labels, tiny badge corners, the edge of a small invoice. MeCard's shorter payload makes a less-dense QR, which scans better at small print sizes. For anything bigger than a postage stamp, use vCard.

faq.q: Do all phones support MeCard?
faq.a: Modern iOS and Android phones do. Some very old Android camera apps don't, but they're rare enough not to matter. If you're in doubt, vCard has wider compatibility.

email.title: Free email QR code generator
email.sub: Open a pre-composed email when scanned, recipient, subject, and body already filled in. The sender just hits send. Great for support cards, contact-us signage, and event flyers.
email.metaDescription: Free email QR code generator, opens a pre-filled email with recipient, subject and body. The sender just taps send. No signup.

faq.q: Does the email send automatically when scanned?
faq.a: No. Scanning opens the user's default mail app with the recipient, subject, and body pre-filled, the user still has to tap Send. That's a safety feature in iOS and Android.

faq.q: Can I include line breaks in the email body?
faq.a: Yes, qr-cow handles the newline escaping for you. Long bodies make the QR denser, so for anything over 200 characters consider linking to a contact form instead.

sms.title: Free SMS QR code generator
sms.sub: Scan to open a pre-composed text message, recipient and message body already filled in. Common for restaurant feedback, two-way SMS surveys, and short-code campaigns.
sms.metaDescription: Free SMS QR code generator, opens a pre-filled text message. Useful for feedback, two-way SMS campaigns, and short-code keyword opt-ins.

faq.q: Does the SMS send automatically?
faq.a: No. The phone opens the default messaging app with the recipient and body pre-filled, the user still confirms before sending. Same safety behaviour as the email QR.

faq.q: Can I use it with an SMS short code?
faq.a: Yes. Enter your short code as the recipient and the keyword (e.g. "PIZZA") as the body. The QR becomes a frictionless way to opt into your SMS campaign.

phone.title: Free phone-call QR code generator
phone.sub: Scan to start a phone call to a number you choose. Useful for taxi-call signs, doctor-appointment cards, real-estate yard signs, and any printed material where "call us" is the next step.
phone.metaTitle: Free Phone Call QR Code Generator
phone.metaDescription: Free phone QR code generator, scan and the dialer opens with your number ready. No signup, no expiration.

faq.q: Does the call start automatically?
faq.a: No, the dialer opens with the number pre-filled, but the user has to tap Call. Phones intentionally don't auto-dial QR codes to prevent abuse.

faq.q: Will country codes work correctly?
faq.a: Yes. Include the full international format (e.g. +44 20 7946 0958) and the QR will dial correctly from anywhere. Without a country code the QR only works inside the same country.

text.title: Free text QR code generator
text.sub: Encode any plain string up to ~4000 characters into a QR, a hidden message, a serial number, a poem, a coupon code, an inventory ID. Whatever the phone reads, the user sees.
text.metaDescription: Free plain-text QR code generator. Encode any string, serial numbers, secret messages, coupon codes, into a scannable QR. No signup.

faq.q: How much text can I fit in one QR code?
faq.a: Around 2,953 characters at error-correction L (the most permissive level), but bigger payloads make a denser code that needs more print area to scan. For more than ~500 characters consider linking to a URL instead.

faq.q: Will the phone open a link if I include 'https://' in the text?
faq.a: Most phones detect URL-shaped strings and offer to open them, even if the QR is plain-text. If you need guaranteed URL-handling, use the URL QR type instead, it sets the URL scheme explicitly.

event.title: Free event QR code generator
event.sub: Add the event to the user's calendar with one tap, title, date, location, and notes pre-filled. Perfect for save-the-dates, conference invites, restaurant pop-ups, and webinar flyers.
event.metaTitle: Free Event / Calendar QR Code Generator
event.metaDescription: Free event QR code generator. Encodes a vEvent that adds the meeting to Google / Apple / Outlook calendar in one tap. No signup.

faq.q: Which calendar apps does the event QR work with?
faq.a: Every major one, Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook, ProtonMail Calendar. The QR encodes the iCalendar (vEvent) standard which all of them parse natively.

faq.q: Can I include a meeting link in the event?
faq.a: Yes, put the Zoom / Meet / Teams link in the notes field. When the user taps the calendar entry their phone makes the link tappable so they can join from the calendar app.

location.title: Free location QR code generator
location.sub: Drop a pin on a map with one scan, latitude + longitude that opens in the phone's maps app. Useful for venue signage, real-estate yard signs, and "find us" flyers.
location.metaTitle: Free Location / GPS QR Code Generator
location.metaDescription: Free location QR code generator, encodes GPS coordinates that open in Apple Maps, Google Maps, or any default maps app. No signup.

faq.q: Will it open in Google Maps or Apple Maps?
faq.a: Whichever is the phone's default. The QR encodes the geo: scheme which both apps register for, iOS picks Apple Maps, Android picks Google Maps unless the user has changed the default.

faq.q: How accurate is the pin?
faq.a: As accurate as the coordinates you supply. Six decimal places gives ~10 cm precision, plenty for the most precise venue pin. Four decimals (~10 m) is fine for most signage.

social.title: Free social-media QR code generator
social.sub: Send scanners straight to your Instagram, TikTok, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, or YouTube profile. Often more reliable than asking strangers to type a handle.
social.metaTitle: Free Social Media QR Code Generator
social.metaDescription: Free social media QR code generator, Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, YouTube. Send scanners straight to your profile in one tap.

faq.q: Will the QR open the app directly or just the website?
faq.a: Most platforms support deep-linking, if the user has the app installed, scanning opens the profile inside the app. Without the app, the QR falls back to the web profile. Either way the user lands on you.

faq.q: What if my handle changes?
faq.a: Static codes encode the link directly, so a handle change means a new QR. If you're likely to rebrand, use a dynamic code pointing at a redirect you can update, the printed QR keeps working forever.

crypto.title: Free crypto wallet QR code generator
crypto.sub: Receive Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, or any other supported coin without typing 42-character addresses. The scanner's wallet app fills the recipient automatically, fewer typos, faster payments.
crypto.metaTitle: Free Crypto Wallet QR Code Generator
crypto.metaDescription: Free crypto wallet QR code generator, receive BTC, ETH, USDT, and more. Removes copy-paste mistakes. No signup.

faq.q: Which wallets are supported?
faq.a: qr-cow generates the standard BIP-21 (Bitcoin), EIP-681 (Ethereum / EVM), and address-only QR formats. They're recognised by every major wallet, MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Phantom, Coinbase Wallet, Exodus, hardware wallets, and the major exchanges.

faq.q: Can I include an amount in the QR?
faq.a: Yes. Bitcoin and Ethereum QRs support an amount field, the scanner's wallet pre-fills the send screen with the value, the user just confirms. Saves a chunk of typing on invoice payments.

faq.q: Use error correction H, is that important?
faq.a: Absolutely. Crypto QRs are the one type where a single misread character can send funds to the wrong address forever. Error correction H means 30% of the modules can be obscured (logo, scratch, smudge) and the code still decodes correctly. Always use H for crypto.

app.title: Free app-store QR code generator
app.sub: Point iOS scanners at the App Store and Android scanners at Google Play, from a single QR. Universal app links resolve automatically based on the user's OS, so the same printed code works for both.
app.metaTitle: Free App Store QR Code Generator
app.metaDescription: Free app store QR code generator, universal link routes iOS to the App Store and Android to Google Play from one QR. No signup.

faq.q: Do I need two different QRs for iOS and Android?
faq.a: Not if you use a universal landing page. qr-cow can generate a single QR that links to a redirect: iOS users land in the App Store, Android users in Google Play. Saves printing two separate codes.

faq.q: Can I track app-install downloads from the QR?
faq.a: Use a dynamic QR plus a deferred-deep-link service (Branch, Adjust, AppsFlyer). The dynamic code lets you change the destination later; the deep-link service attributes installs back to the QR scan.

scanPage.metaTitle: How to scan a QR code, every phone, no app needed
scanPage.metaDescription: Every modern iPhone and Android scans QR codes natively in the camera app. Here's the two-second how-to, plus what to do if it doesn't work.
scanPage.ogDescription: Every modern iPhone and Android scans QR codes natively. Here's how, plus what to do if it doesn't work.
scanPage.h1: You already have a QR scanner. It’s in your camera.
scanPage.intro: Every iPhone since 2017 and every Android since 2019 scans QR codes natively, with no app to install. Here’s how, and what to try if the camera isn’t cooperating.

iosSteps.s1: Open the Camera app (the default one, no extra app needed).
iosSteps.s2: Point the camera at the QR code, no need to tap, just hold steady.
iosSteps.s3: A yellow notification banner appears at the top. Tap it to open the link or action.

androidSteps.s1: Open the Camera app (or pull down the Quick Settings and tap Google Lens).
androidSteps.s2: Point the camera at the QR code.
androidSteps.s3: A pill button appears with the link or action. Tap it.
androidSteps.s4: On Pixel + Samsung phones the Camera detects QR codes automatically. On older Android (≤ 8), use Google Lens or any free scanner app.

noBanner.q: The camera shows the QR but no banner appears.
noBanner.a: Make sure QR scanning is enabled. On iOS: Settings → Camera → Scan QR Codes. On Android: Settings → Apps → Camera → Permissions, and check Google Lens is enabled.

tooSmall.q: The QR is too small or blurry to scan.
tooSmall.a: Hold the phone 15-30 cm away, closer than that and the camera can't focus. If the QR is below ~2 cm wide, ask whoever printed it for a bigger version. Anything under 2 cm × 2 cm is below most cameras' practical resolving power.

onScreen.q: The QR is on my computer screen, can I scan it with my phone?
onScreen.a: Yes. Hold your phone in front of the screen. Glare can throw off the autofocus, angle the screen slightly to kill reflections.

trust.q: I don't trust the link the QR shows.
trust.a: Good instinct. The camera previews the URL before opening, read it. Avoid scanning QR codes in untrusted places (sticker over a parking meter, dropped flyer) and never enter passwords on a page you reached via QR you didn't make yourself.

scanPage.footerNote: qr-cow used to host an in-browser webcam scanner here. We removed it because every phone already does the job better, but if you’re scanning from a laptop without a phone nearby, a free Chrome extension like <link>QR Code Reader</link> works in a pinch. We’re focused on making codes, not reading them.

privacyPage.free2Body: If your browser can't render the styled preview, the encoded string is sent to us once to render a PNG. We log the request with an IP + user-agent for spam-prevention purposes and discard both after 30 days. The encoded content is not stored.

privacyPage.scan1: The QR code id (so we know it's yours).
privacyPage.scan3: Country code, device type (phone / tablet / desktop), and OS family, derived from the scanner's user-agent + IP, not stored as the raw IP itself. We use a coarse IP-to-country lookup and discard the IP immediately.
